title: Projects
description: What the Projects page reads. GET /v1/places is the Swift app's StartPoints list. GET /v1/projects is the Board store's Project catalog, read-only, joined with those places the way ProjectBoardIntegration joins them. GET /v1/projects/:id/worktrees and POST /v1/projects/:id/worktrees/refresh are the worktree lifecycle read model; there is no cleanup route. GET and POST /v1/projects/:id/unify plan and apply one rules file and one skills directory for Claude and Codex (docs/project-files.md, Unify). GET and POST /v1/projects/:id/memory list and add the Project's shared memory; GET, PUT and DELETE /v1/projects/:id/memory/:name show, update and forget one entry (docs/project-memory.md).

StartAvailability.description: AssistantQuota.Availability. This daemon reads no quota, so it answers unknown.

ProjectIconSetup.description: Where this Project's icon comes from. `generated` is the stable path-derived fallback, not a configured identity.

ProjectDeploySetup.description: Whether local workflow-status evidence is connected. This reports configuration, separately from the current run's outcome.

ProjectDeployActivity.description: The current deploy evidence, when a producer has written one. `idle` includes a configured producer with no run worth drawing.

ProjectServerSetup.description: Whether a readable .devstack.json declares at least one server. This is static configuration; it does not probe or start anything.

ProjectSyncSetup.description: Whether an origin repository gives this checkout an identity that another machine can match.

ProjectSetup.description: Cheap, local-only configuration evidence for a Project. It executes no repository command, probes no port and reaches no network.

unify.description: Whether this Project's Claude and Codex sessions read the same rules and skills: the status of the unify plan (GET /v1/projects/:id/unify), read from disk with the same bounded, read-only Plan. Absent from a daemon older than this field, which a console shows as unknown.

unify_count.description: With `unify: drifting`, how many planned changes and conflicts the plan holds; each counts once. Absent otherwise.

StartPlace.description: One directory a session can be started in. `id` is sixteen hex characters of the path's SHA-256 and is the only part a client sends back; `path` is here so two projects with one name can be told apart.

at.description: When this place was last worked in, Unix seconds.

repo.description: The repository this place's checkout clones, host/owner/name from its origin remote, or empty when it has none. Always sent, so a console can tell a machine whose projects have no origin from one whose Clawdline is too old to say. `id` is a digest of a path on this machine, so this is the name one project has on two machines; a schedule is moved between machines by it.

StartPlaceList.description: GET /v1/places: explicitly registered directories, recorded Claude Code folders, Codex rollouts and live sessions' directories, deduplicated, still on disk, newest first, at most forty.

PlaceStarted.description: POST /v1/places/{id}/start[/{assistant}[/{model}][/as/{persona}]]: a terminal was opened and the assistant typed into it. The body is not read. `id` is in the same space as every id in /v1/sessions, but the session is not in that list yet. Needs a device that may send and an Idempotency-Key; a retry within ten minutes is answered from the first reply rather than opening a second tab.

persona.description: The persona the session was launched as, when the path ended `/as/{persona}` (GET /v1/personas); absent for none.

id.description: The new terminal: a tmux pane id or an iTerm2 session id.

assistant.description: claude or codex, as the path named it (claude when it named none).

model.description: The model the path named, or empty.

attach.description: What to type at the Mac to see the session, for the one start that puts it where nobody is looking (a tmux server started detached); empty otherwise.

PlaceResumed.description: POST /v1/places/{id}/resume/[{assistant}/]{session}[/as/{persona}]: a conversation this machine listed for that place, picked back up in a new terminal. The persona form needs the assistant named. The same gate and replay as a start.

persona.description: The persona the resumed session was launched as, when the path ended `/as/{persona}`; absent for none.

PastSession.description: One conversation an assistant has already recorded in a place. `id` is the only part a client sends back.

id.description: A lowercase UUID: the conversation's own id.

at.description: When it was last written to, Unix seconds.

live.description: Something is writing to it right now; resuming it would put a second process on the same record.

PastSessionList.description: GET /v1/places/{id}/sessions[/{assistant}]: what that assistant has recorded in the place, newest first, at most two hundred. Dispatched children and `-p` runs are not conversations and are left out.

more.description: The list stopped at its cap and there were more.

PlaceError.description: A refusal from the start, resume and history routes: not_found, forbidden, bad_request, invalid_launch, terminal_closed, terminal_unsupported, terminal_io_failed, iterm_attention_required, capability_unavailable, terminal_busy, unknown_persona (a start or resume ending `/as/{persona}` that names no persona in GET /v1/personas).

app.description: The terminal the refusal is about, on terminal_closed and iterm_attention_required, so a page can name it in its own language.

CatalogReadStatus.description: ready: the store was read now. stale: the newest read failed and an earlier one is carried. error: nothing could be read.

observedAt.description: Unix seconds of the reading, when there is one.

CatalogIngestion.description: How completely the Board store's own ingestion covered its sources. This daemon does not ingest, so it says unknown.

CatalogProject.description: One Project in the catalog. `label`, `displayPath` and `icon` are present only for a Project a start place resolves to (`isStartPoint`). When the current work-system summary was read, `itemCount` and `activeItemCount` are its complete and open counts and `summaryCoverage` is complete. Otherwise coverage is unknown and consumers ignore both numbers rather than drawing zero.

activeItemCount.description: Open Work System v2 items in this Project.

itemCount.description: Items the current work system files under this Project when its summary was read; otherwise the catalog's historical total.

summaryCoverage.description: Complete when the item counts came from one successful current-store aggregation.

available.description: False when the store could not be read at all; `readState.error` says why.

WorktreeCounts.description: Each is null when any row it sums could not be read, or the observation failed or was truncated. Null is never zero.

WorktreeCleanup.description: An assessment only. No route here acts on it.

WorktreeLifecycle.description: One Project's worktree lifecycle, as ProjectWorktreeLifecycleService.snapshotJSON writes it. Before the first refresh it is `complete: false` with error `not_observed`, which means nobody has looked yet, not that there is nothing.

ProjectUnifyStatus.description: Whether a Project's Claude and Codex sessions read the same rules and skills. `unknown` means something the plan needed could not be read; it is never reported as unified.

ProjectUnifyFileState.description: A rules file at the repository root. `link` is a symbolic link (only CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md counts as an import); `unreadable` could not be read as UTF-8 text within the size limit.

ProjectUnifyReads.description: The rules files each assistant reads, as paths relative to the repository root, following the measured loading rules in docs/shared-project-instructions.md.

claude_imports_agents.description: CLAUDE.md has an `@AGENTS.md` line, or is a link to AGENTS.md.

claude_only_lines.description: Non-blank CLAUDE.md lines other than the import: Codex does not see them. Shown as text; never moved automatically.

claude_only_files.description: Other Claude rules files present (.claude/CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.local.md). Listed, never changed.

ProjectUnifySkillPlace.description: Where a skill is now: only in .agents/skills, only in .claude/skills, in both as one tree (identical copy or already linked), or in both with different content.

ProjectUnifySkill.description: One skill name found in .agents/skills or .claude/skills at the repository root.

copy.description: The two sides are, or will be, separate copies because this machine cannot create links; the check compares them.

action.description: The action that changes this skill; absent when none does (already shared, or a conflict).

ProjectUnifyFileEdit.description: The exact text of one rules file before and after an action. `before` is null when the file is created.

paths.description: Paths relative to the repository root that the action touches.

description.description: One plain sentence for a person.

link_target.description: The relative link a skill_* action creates, as the link spells it.

edits.description: Rules file edits, with exact text. Empty for skill actions.

ProjectUnifyConflict.description: Something unify does not change by itself: the person resolves it. `unreadable` and `too_large` make the plan unknown.

ProjectUnifyPlan.description: GET /v1/projects/:id/unify. Computed from disk at the Project's repository root; reading it writes nothing.

version.description: SHA-256 of every input the plan read. Apply refuses plan_changed when it differs.

links_available.description: False where this machine cannot create symbolic links; skills are then copied (skill_copy).

actions.description: In the order apply performs them.

ProjectMemoryType.description: An entry's kind, the four Claude Code's auto-memory uses.

ProjectMemorySummary.description: One entry as a listing shows it, without its body.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 bytes.

ProjectMemoryEntry.description: One entry in full: the body of POST /v1/projects/:id/memory and of PUT /v1/projects/:id/memory/:name, whose name must be the path's, and the answer to GET /v1/projects/:id/memory/:name.

ProjectMemoryList.description: GET /v1/projects/:id/memory: every entry, and the index a launched session is given. An index cut at its 8 KiB bound says so in index_cut and in its last line; entries always lists every entry.

project_key.description: The repository key the store is filed under: the key the broker names worktree directories by.

index.description: Empty when there are no entries.

ProjectMemoryOutcome.description: What a write did. `unchanged` is the same entry sent again, which is how a retried add or update is answered.

ProjectUnifyApplied.description: The answer to POST /v1/projects/:id/unify. `applied` (200) ran every action; `stopped` (500, with `error` and `detail` as a refusal) ran `ran` and then failed on `failed`. `plan` is recomputed from disk either way.
